name: slide_chord_zero_stagger
description: Slide (back+LK+LP+Block) with all buttons pressed on the same frame

name: slide_chord_two_frame_stagger
description: Slide with LK pressed 2 frames after LP (within CHORD_TOLERANCE=3)

name: slide_chord_five_frame_stagger_still_matches
description: Slide with LK pressed 5 frames after LP, while LP stays held throughout. The chord is satisfied the instant both are simultaneously down (frame 6) -- how far apart their onsets landed is irrelevant, since the game reads button STATE per frame, not press history.
note: Pins rule 1 (simultaneity, no trailing window): a step is satisfied when its full press chord is down AT the current frame, however long ago each class's onset happened, as long as it is still held now.

name: slide_chord_never_overlaps_no_match
description: LP pressed and released (frames 1-2), THEN LK pressed (frames 4-5); Block+back held throughout. LK and LP never share a frame, so the full chord never comes down together -- two separate taps of different classes are two inputs, not one chord.
note: Pins the boundary of rule 1: overlap is required, not just co-occurrence within some window. No overlap ever -> no match, ever.

name: bare_lp_not_chord
description: Bare LP without back direction must NOT match slide chord

name: acid_spit_two_step_gap_within_max
description: Two-step motion (F, gap 6f, F+HP) with gap within MAX_GAP=12

name: acid_spit_gap_exceeds_max
description: Same motion with gap of 13 frames (exceeds MAX_GAP=12, no match)

name: slide_facing_left_resolves_back_correctly
description: When opponent is left (side=-1), 'back' resolves to RIGHT physical button. Slide completes.

name: held_chord_fires_once_not_per_tolerance_window
description: Slide chord held for 11 straight frames. It fires exactly once, on the rising edge where the chord first comes down (frame 1) -- holding the buttons is one slide, not a slide replayed every few frames, so re-firing on a still-held chord would multiply-count a single input in training labels.
note: Pins rule 2 (rising-edge completion + release-based re-arm): a macro completes once when its final step's satisfaction transitions false->true, and only re-arms after that step stops being satisfied.

name: back_to_back_distinct_completions
description: Two separate chord presses (release between them)
